payload.markdown: Attempting to set a value on a constant once it has been declared will cause a parse error. You should use constants when your property needs to be available across all instances of a class, as well as when the property value needs to be fixed and unchanging.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constants: Immutable named values declared with const or define().
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Static & Constants: Members belonging to the class itself rather than to any one instance.
Visibility & Encapsulation: public, protected and private control who may read or write a member.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Constructor Property Promotion: Declaring constructor parameters as properties in a single step (PHP 8).
Dynamic Properties: Creating properties by assignment instead of declaration; deprecated since PHP 8.
